candidates.title: requestDepositWithPermit/requestRedeemWithPermit hard-code the EIP-2612 permit interface on the configurable investment currency
candidates.description: LiquidityPool.requestDepositWithPermit calls ERC20PermitLike(asset).permit(owner,spender,value,deadline,v,r,s) — the 7-arg EIP-2612 shape — directly on the pool's investment currency (`asset`), which is an arbitrary per-pool ERC20. Currencies with a non-standard permit (DAI's allowed/nonce-based permit) or no permit at all revert, making the permit-based deposit/redeem path unusable for those currencies. There is no try/catch, Permit2, or DAI-allowed fallback.

candidates.title: requestDepositWithPermit/requestRedeemWithPermit hard-code EIP-2612 permit on the configurable investment currency
candidates.description: LiquidityPool calls ERC20PermitLike(asset).permit(owner,spender,value,deadline,v,r,s) on the per-pool investment currency. DAI (allowed/nonce-based permit) and no-permit tokens revert -> permit-deposit DoS. No try/catch / Permit2 / DAI-allowed fallback.

candidates.title: ERC4626 convertToShares/convertToAssets are auth-gated (not permissionless views)
candidates.description: InvestmentManager.convertToShares and convertToAssets are declared `public view auth`, so only wards can call them. The ERC4626 standard requires these (and the preview/totalAssets chain that depends on them) to be permissionless views. Integrators calling them directly, and any non-warded caller path, revert — breaking ERC4626 composability.

candidates.title: convertToShares/convertToAssets are auth-gated, breaking ERC4626 permissionless views
candidates.description: InvestmentManager.convertToShares/convertToAssets are `public view auth`; ERC4626 requires permissionless conversion views. Integrators and non-warded paths revert.

candidates.title: Transfer restriction only gates destination membership and members cannot be immediately frozen
candidates.description: RestrictionManager.detectTransferRestriction only checks hasMember(to) (destination), never `from`. updateMember requires block.timestamp <= validUntil, so an admin cannot set validUntil in the past to immediately revoke/freeze an existing member; revocation only takes effect when the existing validUntil expires. Sender-side compliance gating is absent and freezing is delayed.

candidates.title: Transfer restriction checks only destination membership; members cannot be immediately frozen
candidates.description: RestrictionManager.detectTransferRestriction only checks hasMember(to). updateMember requires block.timestamp<=validUntil so validUntil cannot be back-dated to freeze an existing member; revocation waits for natural expiry. Sender-side gating absent.

candidates.title: withApproval modifier contradicts its NatSpec ('owner or authorized admin')
candidates.description: The modifier only permits msg.sender==owner; the documented admin/approval path does not exist. Misleading and blocks delegated flows.

candidates.title: Price/decimal scaling can overflow for unusual tranche decimals (gateway-set, unbounded)
candidates.description: convertToShares uses 10**(PRICE_DECIMALS+trancheTokenDecimals-currencyDecimals). addCurrency bounds currency<=18 but addTranche sets trancheDecimals from the cross-chain message with no bound; large values overflow the scale factor.

candidates.title: Gateway.handle routes upgrade-scheduling and currency/transfer messages with no message-level replay protection
candidates.description: Gateway.handle dispatches incoming router messages (addCurrency, handleTransfer, scheduleRely, etc.) gated only by incomingRouters allowlist and Root pause; there is no per-message nonce/replay guard at this layer (relies entirely on the router). A compromised/mis-added router can drive sensitive flows.

candidates.title: No on-behalf withdraw/redeem: withApproval requires msg.sender == owner despite ERC4626 semantics and NatSpec
candidates.description: LiquidityPool's withApproval(owner) modifier is `require(msg.sender == owner)`. withdraw/redeem(assets,receiver,owner) and requestDeposit/requestRedeem therefore cannot be performed by an ERC20-approved spender/operator, contradicting ERC4626 (approved spender may withdraw owner's assets) and the function NatSpec that claims 'owner or an authorized admin'.

candidates.title: No on-behalf withdraw/redeem despite ERC4626 semantics (withApproval requires msg.sender==owner)
candidates.description: LiquidityPool.withApproval(owner) = require(msg.sender==owner); an approved spender cannot withdraw/redeem on behalf of owner, contradicting ERC4626 and the NatSpec.

candidates.title: convert*/totalAssets quotes use latestPrice with no staleness check
candidates.description: convertToShares/convertToAssets read LiquidityPool.latestPrice(); lastPriceUpdate is written by updatePrice but never validated, so quotes can be based on an arbitrarily stale price. totalAssets() inherits this.

candidates.title: convert*/totalAssets use latestPrice with no staleness check
candidates.description: convertToShares/convertToAssets read latestPrice; lastPriceUpdate is stored but never validated, so quotes can use a stale price. lastPriceUpdate is dead state.

candidates.title: Tranche/LiquidityPool assume the investment currency returns a bool and is non-fee-on-transfer
candidates.description: requestDeposit uses SafeTransferLib.safeTransferFrom for the currency; fee-on-transfer currencies would lock less than the order amount, desyncing the escrowed amount from the gateway invest order.
